title: Why Would Lightning Strike Taller Objects?
description: A science-based story for kids explaining why lightning often strikes taller things.

scenes.narration: Narrator: On a rainy evening in Meghpur, the sky rumbled with thunder and flashes of lightning lit up the night.
scenes.subtitle: Stormy Night

scenes.negative_prompt: blurry, dark, low resolution, distorted, scary, extra limbs

scenes.negative_prompt: blurry, dark, low resolution, distorted, scary, extra limbs
scenes.narration: Tree: Don’t worry, little hut. Lightning usually looks for the tallest path to reach the ground. That might be me!
scenes.subtitle: The Proud Tree

scenes.visual_prompt: (medium shot:1.2) shiny metal tower with friendly face, standing tall, storybook style:1.3
scenes.negative_prompt: blurry, dark, low resolution, distorted, scary, extra limbs
scenes.narration: Tower: Actually, lightning may strike me first. I’m taller, and I’m made of metal which carries electricity easily.
scenes.subtitle: The Confident Tower

scenes.visual_prompt: (medium shot:1.2) wise old cloud with kind eyes, speaking down to hut, tree, and tower, storybook style:1.3
scenes.negative_prompt: blurry, dark, low resolution, distorted, scary, extra limbs
scenes.narration: Cloud: Children, lightning is just electricity trying to reach the ground. It looks for the shortest and easiest path. Taller things are closer, and if they are good conductors, like metal, they attract lightning even more.
scenes.subtitle: The Wise Cloud
scenes.motion_prompt: cloud glowing softly as it speaks

scenes.narration: Narrator: CRACK! A bright bolt shot down! It struck the tower’s lightning rod, which carried the energy safely into the earth. And from that day, the hut, the tree, and the tower understood why lightning loves tall objects… and how science keeps everyone safe.
scenes.subtitle: The Lesson
